loginIntro: Manage VPN infrastructure with deliberate, reviewable changes.
bootstrapHelp: First run: set MVM_ADMIN_USERNAME and MVM_ADMIN_PASSWORD, then run the bootstrap command in your secured terminal. Remove the password variable afterward.
dashboardIntro: An honest view of your inventory, managed identities and provisioning history.
securityIntro: Preview resources and network impact before applying. Existing tunnels remain on RouterOS if this application stops.
singleServer: One managed OpenVPN server per router
mutationsOn: Router writes are enabled. Each operation still requires explicit approval.
mutationsOff: Router writes are disabled. Set MVM_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true only for an authorized lab or deployment.
routerIntro: Connections are tested only on request. Observations older than two minutes are marked stale.
onboardIntro: Register a dedicated REST account. No connection is made until you request a sync or preview.
privateCAHelp: PEM trust anchors for private PKI. System trust is always available; certificate verification cannot be disabled.
ssrfHelp: The administrator must explicitly allow management destination networks using
driftWarning: Configuration changed since the previous observation. Review differences before provisioning; this application does not overwrite external changes automatically.
serverIntro: Only completed, read-back verified jobs appear here. Live interoperability has not been verified.
name: Name
plannedProtocols: OpenVPN, WireGuard, SSTP, L2TP/IPsec and IKEv2 infrastructure have separate forms.
wizardIntro: Complete the settings and save. Commands run after review and final confirmation.
cryptoDefaults: Fixed MVP defaults: TUN, AES-256-CBC, SHA256, TLS 1.2, mandatory client certificate. Advanced combinations require lab validation.
policyHelp: Only these destinations are permitted. Client isolation and default-deny are enforced for the VPN subnet. DNS must be reachable through an allowed destination when inside the tunnel.
firewallWarning: Anchors come from the inspected router, including an explicit empty-chain marker when appropriate. Rules are inserted at the beginning of each chain and checked again before Apply. Review raw/mangle/NAT, FastTrack, existing connections, public exposure, DNS and return routing. No masquerade or full-tunnel Internet access is added.
pkiHelp: A dedicated CA and server certificate will be created and signed on RouterOS. The CA private key stays on the router. You must maintain an authorized encrypted router backup. Certificate identity binding to PPP usernames and effective CRL revocation are not claimed.
impactHelp: The server workflow opens the chosen VPN listener, restricts traffic from the VPN subnet, isolates clients, and generates router-held PKI. Review all rule ordering and routes. Confirm that the endpoint is reachable and the router clock is correct. Read-back verification does not prove client connectivity.
rollbackHelp: On a definite rejected step, compensation removes only previously recorded resources whose current values still match the job. Uncertain responses, changed resources, or interrupted operations require manual review and block subsequent writes. Review dependencies before any manual cleanup. Back up the router before approval.
confirmApply: I reviewed these exact changes, routing, firewall exposure and backup requirements, and authorize this operation.
userIntro: Users are listed separately by service. Disable blocks access; a PPP disconnect alone allows reconnection.
confirmDisable: Authorize credential disable and session termination
passphraseHelp: This passphrase protects the exported client key. Share it separately with the recipient; their VPN client will request it. The profile includes private credentials.
newUserIntro: Each user receives a signed client certificate and a reserved address. Passwords are never embedded in profiles.
autoIPHelp: Leave empty to reserve the next free pool address automatically.
portalAccountHelp: Create the separate end-user login in Settings → Accounts first.
expirationUnavailable: Credential expiration is unavailable. An application database date cannot enforce expiration while the application is offline. Do not treat certificate expiry as PPP credential expiration.
snapshotHelp: On-demand snapshot. A configured account or certificate does not indicate a connected session. No automatic root-cause diagnosis is claimed.
auditHelp: Most recent 200 events. Encrypted application history is not an external tamper-proof audit archive.
deliveryHelp: Sensitive client credentials. This link expires in five minutes and is consumed once. The recipient must sign in as the assigned end user or an authorized VPN administrator. This QR opens a download page; it does not import a VPN configuration automatically.
downloadQR: QR code for authenticated download page
portalHelp: Only profiles assigned to your account are visible. Ask your VPN administrator for a fresh delivery link or credential renewal.
installationHelp: Install an approved OpenVPN client, import the downloaded .ovpn profile, enter your PPP username and password, then the separate client private-key passphrase. Verify the certificate identity and test both permitted and forbidden destinations with your administrator.
noProfiles: No profiles assigned to this account.
clientPending: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS import and connectivity tests: NOT RUN. No client platform is certified yet.
settingsHelp: Configure TLS, database, master key and router destination networks through secured environment configuration. Backups and restores are offline CLI operations. MFA is not implemented.
scopeHelp: Comma-separated inventory router IDs. Empty scopes grant no router access; super administrators have global access.
footer: MikroTik VPN Manager · RouterOS automation experimental · Router and client lab verification pending
noRoutersHelp: Add a router, verify its HTTPS connection, then review its compatibility.
noJobs: No provisioning jobs. Validated previews and operation results will appear here.
previewWarning: WARNING: This application is currently a Development Preview. Real RouterOS and VPN client interoperability testing is incomplete. Production deployment is not recommended.
setupHealth: Encrypted database is accessible. The bootstrap token is available only from the local protected token file.
loopbackOnly: Loopback HTTP only; configure trusted HTTPS before remote exposure.
setupOnboarding: After setup, sign in and optionally register a router from Routers. Registration does not connect or change the router.
publicIPHelp: Required without a domain; used as the IP certificate identity.
wireguardOrder: Execution: validate network → install firewall restrictions → create WireGuard interface and router-generated keys → assign gateway. WireGuard uses keys, not certificates.
serverOnlyHelp: Creates server infrastructure. Client enrollment and profile delivery for this protocol are not available in this panel yet.
domainHelp: Optional, without https:// or a port. Used as the certificate identity.
ikev2Enrollment: IKEv2 identity remains disabled until a client certificate is enrolled and its identity is explicitly restricted. Server infrastructure is saved; this does not create a usable client connection.
monitoringHelp: Colored graphs show up to 120 observed samples per router. Gaps mean unavailable data. Traffic uses physical interface counters; no simulated values are plotted.
certificateOrder: Execution: create CA → sign and verify CA → create server certificate (DNS or IP SAN) → sign and verify → network → firewall → activate server. The private CA must be trusted by clients.
wireguardKeysHelp: A unique WireGuard key pair is generated for this peer. No PPP password is needed.
wireguardExportHelp: Download a .conf file or scan the native WireGuard QR.
autoMonitor: Collect every 30 seconds while this page is visible (authorized routers only)
wireguardQRHelp: Scan this QR directly in WireGuard to import the configuration. It contains the client private key; keep it private. The file download link expires after five minutes.
l2tpOrder: Execution: create address pool and PPP profile → install IPsec access and plaintext L2TP drop rules → verify firewall order → enable L2TP with required IPsec.
pppUserHelp: Set credentials specific to this PPP service and reserve a client IP address.
natOutputHelp: Choose the intended output interface, for example ether1 or pppoe-out1.
networkAdminOnly: Router administrator permission is required to change NAT and firewall rules.
natOnly: NAT only; forwarding rules are unchanged
networkIntro: Choose an existing output interface and source range on the selected router, then review the commands before applying.
existingRangesHelp: Completed VPN servers, router pools, and interface networks. Pool ranges are used exactly without including outside addresses.
networkPolicyHelp: Only the selected range and output interface are targeted. Masquerade excludes outbound IPsec traffic. Client configuration routes are not changed.
chooseRouterForNetwork: Select a router and load its existing interfaces and ranges first.
allowSelectedForward: Also permit this range through the selected interface and allow established return traffic
networkChoicesMissing: No usable source range or enabled interface is available. Create one on the router or in Servers, then reload the selections.
networkForwardUnavailable: The first forward rule is dynamic. NAT-only is available; forwarding changes require order review.
routerSimpleIntro: Enter the router connection details. Saving automatically tests the connection.
hostOnly: IP or hostname only; no https:// or port.
wwwSSLHelp: The www-ssl HTTPS port on MikroTik, usually 443.
sharedUsersIntro: One user, multiple services. Manage credentials and configuration files together.
sharePPPCredentials: Use this username and password across all managed PPP services on this router
sharedPPPHelp: Shared OpenVPN, SSTP and L2TP use one PPP account and IP policy. If OpenVPN exists, its address pool and access policy are used. WireGuard configuration can be added to the same user afterwards. Other PPP listeners must be disabled.
confirmDisableAll: Disable this user across all linked services
stepCreateSharedUser: Create a shared user and get configurations
noAvailableServices: No additional service is available. Create the desired VPN servers first; existing user services are listed under Users.
